_transcription: Bilingual booklet, 27 pages (idx 0-26), matching the cover's 'contains 27 printed pages'. Hindi FIRST then English throughout: idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions, then ENGLISH on every EVEN index 2-26 and Hindi on every ODD index 3-25. Walked all 27 indices; no English overflow sits on any odd page, there is no parity inversion, and idx 26 (English, Q33 d-g) is the final page. The paper's own General Instructions confirm the full70 shape exactly: 33 questions, five sections, A 1-16 @1, B 17-21 @2, C 22-28 @3, D 29-30 case @4, E 31-33 @5 = 70. Instruction (viii) prints NO internal-choice count, so the OR roster was built by walking the marking scheme for a bare OR on its own line and confirming each against a printed OR on the paper: Q17, Q29(c), Q30(c), Q31, Q32 = five. DECIMALS ARE RAISED DOTS on this paper, read at 3x magnification on Q5's options (0.54/0.46/0.92/0.27 all sit mid-digit-height), so written as 0{\cdot}54. Section-A answers are verbatim from the official marking scheme for QP CODE 56/1/2 (ms/p02.png), read by vision because keys.ts cannot extract this scheme; all 16 letters re-read at 3x. Note the scheme's own heading misprints the year as 'MARKING SCHEME 2023' while its cover page says Senior School Certificate Examination, 2024 — the QP code, every question and the Section-A key all match this 2024 paper, so the heading is a CBSE typo, not the wrong document. Its title block reads Q.P.CODE 56_1_1,2,3 but the answer pages carry 'QP CODE 56/1/2' and its numbering matches THIS set (scheme Q29 = crystal field, Q30 = batteries, as printed here), so no renumbering hazard applies. Whole scheme scanned for voids across all 9 pages: exactly ONE, at Q4, unconditional and applying to BOTH language editions (the Hindi Q4 at idx 3 prints the same defective structures). Overlap with opener 56/1/1 matched on CONTENT, never position: 25 of 42 rows are the same question and 17 are new. Section D is SWAPPED (this paper's Q29 is the opener's Q30 and vice versa) and Section E is rotated (31<-33, 32<-31, 33<-32), while Section A is almost entirely fresh (only Q10 and Q13 recur) and Section C is a straight reshuffle in which all seven recur. The 25 reuse the opener's text byte-for-byte after confirming each on this paper's own page, so they dedup at commit; verified programmatically on stem + sorted option texts + answer + context, with no near-miss pairs and no key disagreement on any shared row.

questions.context: The Valence Bond Theory (VBT) explains the formation, magnetic behaviour and geometrical shapes of coordination compounds whereas 'The Crystal Field Theory' for coordination compounds is based on the effect of different crystal fields (provided by ligands taken as point charges), on the degeneracy of d-orbital energies of the central metal atom/ion. The splitting of the d-orbitals provides different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields. The crystal field theory attributes the colour of the coordination compounds to d-d transition of the electron. Coordination compounds find extensive applications in metallurgical processes, analytical and medicinal chemistry.

questions.context:
Batteries and fuel cells are very useful forms of galvanic cell. Any battery or cell that we use as a source of electrical energy is basically a galvanic cell. However, for a battery to be of practical use it should be reasonably light, compact and its voltage should not vary appreciably during its use. There are mainly two types of batteries — primary batteries and secondary batteries.
In the primary batteries, the reaction occurs only once and after use over a period of time the battery becomes dead and cannot be reused again, whereas the secondary batteries are rechargeable.
Production of electricity by thermal plants is not a very efficient method and is a major source of pollution. To solve this problem, galvanic cells are designed in such a way that energy of combustion of fuels is directly converted into electrical energy, and these are known as fuel cells. One such fuel cell was used in the Apollo space programme.
questions.stem: How do primary batteries differ from secondary batteries ?

(iii) Why are equimolar solutions of sodium chloride and glucose not isotonic ?
questions._flag: Sub-part (i) is 'Vapour Pressure of Liquid Solutions' (2 marks); the row is filed on 'Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass', which covers (ii) and (iii) together, i.e. 2+1=3 of the printed 2+2+1=5.

questions.stem:
Answer any five questions of the following :
(a) N,N-diethyl-benzenesulphonamide is insoluble in alkali. Give reason.
(b) Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction. Why ?
(c) Write a simple chemical test to distinguish between methylamine and aniline.
(d) Write the chemical reaction involved in Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.
(e) How will you convert aniline to p-bromoaniline ?
(f) Complete the following reaction :
Benzenediazonium chloride \(\xrightarrow[\mathrm{(ii)\ NaNO_2\,/\,Cu,\ \Delta}]{\mathrm{(i)\ HBF_4}}\)
(g) Write the structures of A and B in the following reaction :
Benzoic acid \(\xrightarrow[\Delta]{\mathrm{NH_3}} \mathrm{A} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Br_2 + NaOH}} \mathrm{B}\)
questions._flag: Seven sub-parts of which the student answers any five, at 1 mark each. All seven are Amines chemistry but they straddle three subtopics — (d) and (g) are 'Preparation of Amines' (Gabriel phthalimide, Hofmann bromamide), (f) is 'Chemical Reactions of Diazonium Salts', and the remaining four are 'Chemical Reactions of Amines', on which the row is filed as the majority. A single row, because there is no OR branch to ingest.
questions._figure: ILLUSTRATIVE — Two sub-parts print DRAWN structures as their starting material rather than naming it: (f) a Kekule benzene hexagon bearing \(\mathrm{N_2^+Cl^-}\), and (g) a Kekule benzene hexagon bearing \(\mathrm{COOH}\); both rings verified at 4x as carrying three inner double-bond lines, so both are benzene and not a plain saturated hexagon. They are named in words above because the answers asked for are the products, so naming the substrates leaks nothing; the real crops should still be attached. Page idx 26.
